claim: Gion private-alley no-entry signs were installed at Kosode Koji on May 29, 2024, carrying a fine of up to ¥10,000, and observers reported tourists were broadly complying.
quote: Private Road Do Not Enter Fine up to ¥10,000 ... When Japanese outlets checked compliance, nobody was seen entering the road

claim: Tourists remain free to walk Hanami-koji, Shirakawa Minami, Yasaka Shrine, and Pontocho; the ban targets only private side alleys in Gion.
quote: everyone still has access to the district's main street, Hanami Koji ... Shirakawa Minami, all the main temples including Yasaka Shrine, Pontocho Alley

claim: Higashiyama's core walk between Kiyomizu-dera and Yasaka Shrine is about 2 km but typically a half-day with stops; shops open ~9-10 and close ~17-18.
quote: shops typically open around nine or ten in the morning and close relatively early around five or six in the evening

claim: The classic Yasaka Pagoda streetscape shot is from the middle of Yasaka-dori between Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka; aim for 6-9 AM or golden hour to avoid crowds.
quote: aim for early mornings (around 6-9 AM) or late evenings, with many visitors finding the golden hour before sunset offers magical lighting

claim: Pontocho is dead by day but transforms into Kyoto's most atmospheric street in the evening; the lane bans cars, modern buildings, and gaudy signs.
quote: By day, it's not much to look at. But in the evening, Pontocho becomes a magical place ... no cars, modern buildings or gaudy signs are allowed

claim: Pontocho stretches ~500 m between Sanjo and Shijo, walkable end-to-end in 10 minutes, with 6-9 PM the sweet spot for lantern light and maiko sightings.
quote: The alley stretches approximately 500 meters between Sanjo-dori in the north and Shijo-dori in the south, and a leisurely walk from end to end takes no more than 10 minutes

claim: Enter the Arashiyama bamboo grove through Tenryu-ji's north gate to skip the worst crowds, then continue to Okochi-Sanso Villa (admission includes matcha) and loop back via Kameyama-koen and the Katsura riverside.
quote: entering via Tenryu-ji Temple's north exit helps you skip the worst of the crowds ... superb villa and garden is well worth a visit. Your admission ticket includes matcha tea and a sweet

claim: The bamboo path is best walked before 8 AM, when the famous rustling soundscape is audible and crowds are absent; the grove is free and open 24 hours.
quote: before 8:00 AM, when the path is empty, the morning light filters dramatically through the bamboo, and you can actually hear the famous rustling sound

claim: The Philosopher's Path is a ~2 km canal-side stone walk from Ginkaku-ji to Nanzen-ji, peaking in early April with cherry blossoms; named for Nishida Kitaro who meditated en route to Kyoto University.
quote: approximately two kilometers, beginning near Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion) and concluding in the Nanzenji neighborhood ... philosopher Nishida Kitaro, who was said to practice meditation while walking this route

claim: Honen-in (free entry, mossy thatched gate) is the standout less-obvious stop along the Philosopher's Path, and the path links easily to Eikan-do and Nanzen-ji's aqueduct at the southern end.
quote: Honen-in Temple stands out with an entrance gate that is quite spectacular especially during the autumn

claim: Nishiki Market is a five-block covered shopping street with 100+ shops and the etiquette rule that eating-while-walking is bad manners locally; shops generally run 10:00-18:00.
quote: Refrain from eating while walking. This is considered bad manners and a major nuisance by local shoppers.

claim: Nishiki sits in downtown Kyoto bracketed by the Teramachi and Shinkyogoku covered arcades, making it easy to extend a market visit into Kawaramachi-Karasuma shopping.
quote: surrounded by Teramachi and Shinkyogoku shopping arcades that run alongside the market offering everything from modern boutiques to centuries-old specialty stores

claim: Tatsumi Bridge over the Shirakawa is the most photographed spot in northern Gion (used in Memoirs of a Geisha) and is best at dawn or after dark with lanterns; the alley is narrow and jams up by mid-morning.
quote: Tatsumi Bridge on Shirakawa River is one of the famous bridges in the Gion district because of a scene from the movie 'Memoirs of a Geisha'
